newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe sees solution in U.S.-French NATO row.
newsitem.headline: Juppe sees solution in U.S.-French NATO row.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Tuesday it was possible to solve a row with the United States over the nationality of a regional commander that is holding up the alliance reform.
But he repeated that Paris insisted on "Europeanising" regional commands, which highlights French desires for a strong European identity in the transatlantic alliance.

"There are some problems to settle, particularly the issue of Europeanising regional commands which France sees as essential," Juppe said at a party for members of NATO's parliamentary assembly meeting in Paris.
"We must solve these difficulties. I am convinced this is possible," he said.
France, as part of its watershed decision to return to NATO's military structure, wants the commander of southern European forces (AFSOUTH) based in Naples, to be a European.
Washington insists the job, which controls the U.S. Sixth Fleet in the Mediterranean should remain, as it always has, in American hands.

Military chiefs of staff from the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation are to meet in Brussels on November 21-22 to make recommendations to the alliance's political leaders on how NATO should work in the future.

NATO officials have said the U.S.-French row would mean no accord on a new command structure. Discussion has centred on whether to cut back on the number of regional commands, which now number three in the Atlantic and three in Europe.
